chapter: Trumpeters he admired and the Ellington near-miss
title: Artie Whetsol's "Mood Indigo" sound and Ray Nance
summary: Nobody sounded like Whetsol on "Mood Indigo"; Dance says only Ray Nance sometimes recalled his delicate, soulful tone, perhaps because he was a violinist.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah, I always like his style. That was strictly him, you know, it was him. And [Artie] Whetsol -- even Whetsol, in the band. Who could sound like Whetsol playing "Mood Indigo."
When they'd bring them three down front.
Yeah. I mean a lot of guys have played it, but I mean for some reason unknown, I don't know --
You know, I think the only guy that would recall Whetsol at any time would have been Ray Nance sometimes.
You know, because Whetsol had that very soulful and delicate thing.
Which Ray would -- I suppose maybe because he was a violinist.
Yeah. Yeah, that could have something to do with it, yeah.
Then he would come up with that. Duke
Oh, that guy was something else.
